name: Search memories
summary: Ask a question in your own words and get back the memories that answer it.
description: Matching is on meaning, not keywords, so the query works best as the question your feature is actually trying to answer rather than the words you expect to find.

params.name: graph_id
params.note: Which graph to search. A key pinned to one graph may omit it.

params.name: query
params.note: Natural language search query.

params.name: limit
params.note: Maximum memories to return. Defaults to 5, and anything above 100 is clamped to 100.

params.name: format
params.note: markdown, the default, is prompt-ready text. json returns structured items instead.

params.name: context_ids
params.note: Narrows: results are restricted to these contexts.

params.name: boost_context_ids
params.note: Widens: also pulls in memories linked to these contexts.

params.name: context_types
params.note: Filter by type. Keys are type names, values are arrays of context names.

params.name: sources
params.note: Filter by provenance tier, for example ["verified", "tool"].

params.name: expand_depth
params.note: How many levels of links to follow. Defaults to 1.

returns: A rendered string by default. With `format: "json"` you get `items` instead of `memories`.

errors.note: The body was not valid JSON, or a field failed its check. The message names the field.
No key, or a key that has been revoked.
The key is pinned to a different graph. A key cannot widen itself.

name: Deep recall
summary: One call for questions a single search cannot answer.
description: Walks the graph rather than matching once, then answers in prose with the evidence behind it. Check `coverage` and `fallback` before trusting the summary: both shapes still return one, and both still cost you.

params.name: graph_id
params.note: Which graph to walk.

params.name: question
params.note: One focused question. Not a conversation, and not three questions joined by "and also".

params.name: context_ids
params.note: Contexts you already believe are relevant, to start the walk from.

returns: `summary` in prose, `facts` as the evidence, and `coverage` saying whether the walk finished.

name: Store an event
summary: Write one thing your app learned.
description: Address it with a stable `context_id` in `type:name` form so repeated mentions of the same thing accrete on one node and can be reinforced or corrected later.

params.name: graph_id
params.note: Which graph to write to.

params.name: event_kind
params.note: What sort of memory this is.

params.name: context_id
params.note: The stable address, in `type:name` form, for example `preference:dark_mode`.

params.name: source
params.note: Provenance, which sets how far the memory is trusted. The ladder runs from policy down to system.

params.name: payload
params.note: The memory itself. Put a concise natural-language statement in `payload.data`: that is the text search matches on.

params.name: related_to
params.note: Associated context ids, in `type:name` form.

params.name: extends
params.note: Contexts this memory adds detail to.

params.name: reinforces
params.note: Contexts this memory supports with new evidence.

params.name: contradicts
params.note: Contexts this memory conflicts with.

returns: The stored memory's id.

name: Send an observation
summary: Propose a memory instead of writing one.
description: An observation is not a write with a flag on it. What comes back is an id, not a memory: the engine distils a statement from the payload and a person approves or rejects it before anything is stored.

params.name: graph_id
params.note: Which graph the finding would be filed in.

params.name: source
params.note: Where this came from. `derived` is refused: the engine never re-observes its own output.

params.name: payload
params.note: The raw observation, stored verbatim. Capped at 64KB; whole documents belong to ingest.

params.name: stream
params.note: A name that keeps concurrent workflows apart. Capped at 256 bytes.

params.name: observed_at
params.note: When the observed thing happened, in unix seconds. No earlier than 2020, no more than a day ahead.

returns: `observation_id`, with a 202. Nothing is stored yet.
